title: Lesson 60: Presenting AI System Designs with the Same Review Skills

questions.question: A reviewer wants to judge whether an AI agent design will actually work. What should the presenter lead with?
options: A live demonstration of the agent answering several representative prompts.
An evaluation plan showing the evidence it works and where it is thin.
A single accuracy score computed on one curated dataset.
A list of platform features the design depends on.
questions.explanation: An AI system has no single behavior to demonstrate, only an expected behavior that is as trustworthy as the evaluation behind it. So the presenter leads with how the behavior was measured and where the evidence is weak.

questions.question: System logs mark an agent session as successful, yet reading the transcript shows the user never got their task done. What does this illustrate?
options: A P0 trust-breaking failure, because the agent gave a flatly wrong answer.
A benign artifact, because the log is the source of truth.
A phantom success, where the log reports a win the user did not get.
A model-layer regression, because the underlying model changed.
questions.explanation: This is a phantom success: telemetry reports a win that the user did not experience. It is why an AI review cannot stop at the logs and must count whether the user actually got what they needed.

questions.question: A board asks how the design prevents an agent from calling the wrong tool or endpoint. What is the strongest answer?
options: Show the written tool schemas, descriptions, and selection tests.
Rely on the model to choose the correct tool without added guidance.
Restrict the agent to a single tool so no wrong choice is possible.
Trust the outcome-layer evaluation, since final results confirm correctness.
questions.explanation: Tool selection depends on the contract between the model and each tool. Clear schemas and semantic descriptions, plus an evaluation that exercises selection under realistic inputs, are what keep the agent from invoking irrelevant tools.
